0.long_answer: In newborns with certain anorectal malformations, such as imperforate anus, a temporary colostomy is typically performed within the first day or two of life. This procedure involves creating an artificial opening (stoma) in the abdomen, which diverts stool away from the malformed or absent anal opening. This allows the infant to pass stool safely while postponing definitive corrective surgery until the child is larger and better able to tolerate more complex reconstruction.
